html:
The Sinixt, or Lakes people, are an Interior Salish people of the upper Columbia River and the Arrow Lakes, in what is now south-eastern British Columbia and north-eastern Washington. Their language is a dialect of the Okanagan-Colville language, shared with the Syilx.

They lived from salmon, caught at Kettle Falls and other places on the Columbia, and from the forests and lakes around them. After the border of 1846 split their land, epidemics and settlement pushed most of them south to the Colville Reservation in Washington. In 1956 Canada declared the Sinixt in Canada extinct. A Sinixt man from Washington challenged this by hunting in British Columbia, and in 2021, in R v Desautel, the Supreme Court of Canada ruled that the Sinixt still hold Aboriginal rights there.
